brief.subject: State tax ballot fights heat up in Colorado, Florida, California
brief.headline: State Tax Measures Head to Voters in Colorado, Florida and California
brief.dek: Colorado weighs several overlapping tax measures, Florida's property tax amendment looks close, and the IRS Advisory Council schedules a public meeting.
brief.lede: Tax questions are on several state ballots, and the results could change what owners pay locally. Colorado alone has four tax-related measures that interact with one another.

sections.heading: Colorado's Stacked Tax Ballot
bullets: Amendment 87 and propositions NN, 136 and 137 all address taxes or tax refunds, each in a different way.
How they combine depends on which pass, so owners should watch the full set rather than any single measure.
The income tax proposal has faced bipartisan criticism and survived a legal challenge, signaling a contested vote.

sections.heading: Florida Property Tax Vote Looks Tight
bullets: The amendment needs 60% support to pass, a high bar for any ballot measure.
Only one poll so far has shown it reaching that level, and polling overall is limited.
Property owners and commercial tenants should plan for either outcome until results are in.

sections.heading: California Billionaire Tax Goes Social
bullets: California voters are deciding whether to impose a special tax on billionaires.
Paid social media influencers are increasingly involved in campaigning on the measure, so expect heavy online messaging.
The tax targets billionaires, not typical small businesses, but it shapes the state's broader tax debate.

sections.heading: IRS Advisory Council to Meet Publicly
bullets: The Internal Revenue Service Advisory Council has announced a public meeting in the Federal Register.
These sessions can preview IRS priorities, so bookkeepers and tax pros may want to track the agenda.
